title: Hatch Duty
setup: One of the family has slept sitting against the hatch for three nights, listening. Nobody else has slept much either.

options.label: Take the hatch in shifts with them
options.outcome: Two hours on, two hours off, all night. Nobody hears anything. That seems to help.

options.label: Talk it through until morning
options.outcome: {name} sits up and hears every reason the hatch isn't safe. By morning there are fewer of them.

options.label: Let them keep watch alone
options.outcome: The watch goes on. The whole shelter sleeps with one ear on the hatch.

title: The Ledger
setup: One of the family has started a written list of who ate what, and reads it aloud at dinner.

options.label: Put them in charge of the shelf
options.outcome: The ledger becomes the official inventory. Portions get very precise. Nobody else enjoys it, but the reading aloud stops.

options.label: Have it out at dinner
options.outcome: It's loud, then it's quiet, then somebody passes the {food_label}. That might be the end of it.

options.label: Play cards for first pick of the cans
options.outcome: The cards settle it: the winner picks first all week. The ledger gets turned over and used as a scorecard.

title: Facing the Wall
setup: One of the family hasn't spoken since yesterday. They're sitting facing the wall, very still.

options.label: Sit with them, saying nothing
options.outcome: {name} sits beside them all afternoon. Neither says a word. Near dusk, a hand reaches over and stays there.

options.label: Give them one small job
options.outcome: Fold the blankets. Just that. The blankets get folded, or they don't.

options.label: Leave the console beside them

alt.label: Leave the sock puppets beside them

effects.what: a thumb found the power button

options.outcome: The console sits there an hour before a thumb finds the power button. Then the quiet beeping starts, and keeps going.

title: Boots On
setup: One of the family is lacing their boots at dawn, with a bag packed for the farthest place on the map.

options.label: Walk with them to the corner and back
options.outcome: Two people, one block, a lot of dust. They come back down the ladder breathing hard and a little steadier.

options.label: Hide the boots
options.outcome: The boots go behind the water heater. Nobody leaves today. Nobody is speaking to whoever hid them, either.

options.label: Plan a nearer trip together on the map
options.outcome: The map comes out and two fingers argue across it. They settle on somewhere closer, with a pencil line home.

title: No Questions Asked
setup: A notice on the lamp post, in neat capitals: things went missing from houses on this street. No questions if they come back.

options.label: Leave a can under the notice
options.outcome: One can of {food_label}, set down under the notice after dark. It isn't what was taken. It's what there is.

options.label: Walk past it

effects.text: The notice on the lamp post is gone. Nobody in the shelter asks who took it down.

options.outcome: Everyone reads it. Nobody mentions it. That takes a surprising amount of effort.

options.label: Leave a medkit under the notice

effects.what: left under the notice on the lamp post

options.outcome: The medkit goes under the notice after dark. By morning it's gone. A day later, so is the notice.

title: The Long Way Home
setup: {name}'s route home passes a house the family would rather not think about. There's a light in one window now.

options.label: Take the long way round
options.outcome: Three extra blocks through the dust, so as not to see the window. {name} gets home late and says the street was blocked.

options.label: Walk past, head down
options.outcome: {name} walks past without looking. It's a short street. It takes a long time.

options.label: Leave a can on their step
options.outcome: {name} sets a can on the step, knocks once, and is round the corner before the door opens. It doesn't fix anything.

title: Midnight Snack
setup: {subject} is at the food shelf at 3 a.m. with a spoon and an open can. The rules wall says kids eat last.

options.label: Let them finish it
options.outcome: Nobody saw anything. Two rations of {food_label} are missing from the count, and the rules wall looks less sure of itself.

options.label: Put the lid back on, gently
options.outcome: {name} puts the can back and walks {subject} to bed. Rules are rules. Neither of them sleeps.

options.label: Split your own ration with them
options.outcome: {name} sits on the floor and splits the can, spoon for spoon. Technically, the kid ate last.

title: A Knock Anyway
setup: An old man is at the hatch asking for water for his wife. The rules wall says nobody opens the hatch.

options.label: Open the hatch and give him a bottle
options.outcome: The hatch opens for the first time in days. He takes the bottle in both hands.

options.label: Pass water out through the vent
options.outcome: Two rations go out through the vent in a bag on a string. The rule holds. He says thank you to the vent.

options.label: Keep to the rule
options.outcome: He knocks for a while, then stops. The rules wall gets looked at a lot that evening.

title: What Counts as Work
setup: {subject} says sitting up all night watching the vent counts as work. The rules wall doesn't define work.

options.label: It counts
options.outcome: {subject} eats. By evening, three other people have taken up vent-watching.

options.label: It doesn't count
options.outcome: {subject} goes without and refuses tomorrow's trip on principle. The vent goes unwatched.

options.label: Write a definition on the wall
options.outcome: The definition runs to three sub-clauses and a footnote. Everyone has a job now, mostly arguing about the footnote.
